stem: Describe the main features of the Great Leap Forward.

points.description: Aim to overtake Britain's industry within about fifteen years by mass mobilisation.
People's communes replaced collectives; private plots abolished.
Communal kitchens.
Backyard furnaces produced much useless steel; farm work neglected.
Unscientific farming methods / sparrow campaign.
Exaggerated harvest reports; state grain procurement led to famine.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Mao aimed to overtake Britain's industrial output within about fifteen years by mobilising the people. Collectives were merged into huge people's communes, private plots were abolished and families ate in communal kitchens. Millions made steel in backyard furnaces, much of it useless, while farm work was neglected. Unscientific methods such as close planting and the campaign against sparrows reduced harvests. Officials reported false harvests, and the state took grain on that basis, which led to famine.

hints: Cover aims, organisation, methods and outcome.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why Mao launched the Cultural Revolution in 1966.

points.description: Identifies wish to regain power after the Great Leap failures.
Explains: Liu Shaoqi and Deng had led the recovery and Mao was sidelined.
Identifies wish to purge "capitalist roaders" / keep revolutionary spirit alive.
Explains: he feared the Party was becoming bureaucratic and moving away from socialism, as he believed had happened in the USSR.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: After the disaster of the Great Leap Forward, Liu Shaoqi and Deng Xiaoping led the recovery and Mao was sidelined, so he used the Cultural Revolution to regain control and remove them. He also feared that the Party was becoming bureaucratic and moving towards capitalism, as he believed had happened in the Soviet Union, so he mobilised young people to attack "capitalist roaders" and keep the revolution alive.

hints: Consider Mao's position after the famine and his fears about the Party.

Study the source and answer the questions.

**Source A** — a poster of the kind displayed in Chinese villages in 1958, described in words (described in words; invented for this question)

> Smiling peasants stand beside a mountain of golden grain taller than a house. Behind them, the chimneys of small furnaces glow red and a banner reads "Overtake Britain in fifteen years". A child holds up an enormous ear of wheat.

parts.label: (a)

parts.label: (b)

points.description: Purpose: propaganda to mobilise peasants for the Great Leap.
Detail: smiling peasants and giant harvests suggest success and enthusiasm.
Context: launch of communes and backyard furnaces in 1958.
Context: the slogan of overtaking Britain set ambitious targets.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: How far does Source A give an accurate picture of the Great Leap Forward? Use the source and your own knowledge.

points.description: Accurate: shows real aims (grain, steel, overtaking Britain) and the backyard furnaces.
Accurate: mass mobilisation and enthusiasm in 1958.
Inaccurate: harvests fell; much furnace steel was useless.
Inaccurate: false reporting and procurement led to famine (estimates about 15-45 million deaths).
Provenance: propaganda, made to inspire, not to inform.
Supported judgement.

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant factors or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
The poster accurately shows the aims of the Great Leap: huge harvests, steel from backyard furnaces and the slogan of overtaking Britain within fifteen years. In 1958 there was real mass mobilisation.

But as a picture of results it is very misleading. Harvests fell because of the steel campaign, close planting and other unscientific methods, and much of the furnace steel was useless. Officials reported false harvests, the state took grain on that basis, and a famine followed in which historians estimate that between about 15 and 45 million people died.

The poster was propaganda, designed to inspire effort, not to inform. It is accurate about the aims but not about what actually happened.

explanation: Source-based practice question on the Great Leap Forward (12 marks).
hints: Think about the poster's purpose and what actually happened.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
Mao's rule brought real gains. China was unified and independent after a century of foreign domination and civil war. Land reform ended landlord power and gave land to some 300 million peasants. The First Five-Year Plan built heavy industry, China tested an atomic bomb in 1964 and took the UN seat in 1971. The Marriage Law improved women's legal status, literacy rose, barefoot doctors brought basic care to villages, and life expectancy rose substantially.

The harm, however, was immense. Land reform killed perhaps one to two million or more landlords. The Great Leap Forward caused a famine in which historians estimate between about 15 and 45 million people died. Critics were silenced in the Anti-Rightist Campaign, and the Cultural Revolution brought ten years of persecution and disrupted education. The cult of personality meant that Mao's mistakes could not be challenged.

The Party's own verdict in 1981 was that his achievements outweighed his mistakes, but many historians disagree. In my judgement the scale of the deaths, especially in the famine, means that I do not fully agree, even though the social and economic changes were real.

parts.explanation: Both sides with a supported judgement.

hints: In (b), weigh achievements against human costs.
